newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia calls for more export-oriented activity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia calls for more export-oriented activity.

text.p: Indonesian central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Wednesday domestic banks should make sure that foreign loans were used for export-oriented activities.

"I would like to remind all banks receiving foreign loans to ensure that the loans are genuinely used for productive and particularly export-oriented activities," he told bank leaders at an industry dinner.

Djiwandono said the more domestic investment depended on foreign financing, the greater the risks for the national economy even though Indonesia needed foreign funds to cover its savings-investment gap and the current account deficit.

"These risks become particularly acute when the capital inflows consist of short-term, speculative funds," he said. "We must therefore endeavour to make the capital inflows stay for the long term and this can be done by consistently improving the fundamentals of the economy."
Coordinating Minister for Economy and Finance Saleh Affif said on Monday that non-oil exports were expected to rise by 14.2 percent in fiscal 1997/98 (April/March).
Affif said non-oil exports in the coming year were expected to rise by 14.2 percent, while total exports were estimated to rise by 8.6 percent.
Djiwandono also said that banks would be encouraged to make more effective and efficient use of risk management.

"In line with the principles of self-regulatory banking, Bank Indonesia is endeavouring to improve the soundness in bank rating regulations, particularly in the evaluation of banking management which will give more weight to management quality and performance," he added.
